analysis.title: Seagate Technology (STX): Solid quarter relative to elevated expectations; shifting industry dynamics likely to cap HDD multiples
key_insights: GS expects STX to trade modestly lower on an essentially in-line quarter and stronger guidance, because expectations were elevated after a strong Western Digital report.

Investor conversations show mixed positioning going into the print. Supply and demand in HDD are tight and mix is improving toward higher-capacity drives, but a smaller competitor could add significant capacity.

Management said customer demand will stay elevated for the foreseeable future. It implicitly acknowledged that competitors (GS believes Toshiba) could ramp units, but said this is highly unlikely to disrupt industry supply/demand balance.
GS keeps a Buy rating. Strong incremental margins, helped by the HAMR technology ramp, should drive outsized earnings growth over the coming year.
FQ1 (3Q26 column) revenue was $4.23bn vs GS $4.20bn and Street $4.14bn. Gross margin was 57.8% vs GS 57.2% and Street 57.6%. Non-GAAP EPS was $7.68 vs GS $7.59 and Street $7.42.
Data Center revenue was $3.45bn vs GS $3.40bn and Street $3.39bn. Edge IoT revenue was $784mn vs GS $794mn and Street $767mn.
Exabyte shipments grew 21% y/y. Management expects growth to re-accelerate in the December quarter and reach ~25% in the medium term.
Price per exabyte rose ~33% y/y, and management expects this pricing trend to last through FY27. Management also expects sequential quarterly increases in revenue and margins through fiscal 2027.

Seagate is ramping Mozaic 4 (HAMR) production with two hyperscalers and plans to qualify more customers in coming months. HAMR volume is still expected to cross over PMR by the end of calendar 2026. GS expects HAMR to be ~70% of shipments in CY27.
Mozaic 5 is expected to be in qualification at key customers by the end of CY27. Seagate has developed joint solutions with Broadcom for customers including Microsoft.

Seagate retired ~$775mn of debt in the quarter and paid down another $750mn of senior notes after quarter end. It expects to be net cash positive by the end of CY26 and to significantly increase buybacks starting in CY27.

FQ2 guidance is above the Street. Revenue midpoint is $4.80bn vs GS $4.60bn and Street $4.50bn. Operating EPS midpoint is $9.20 vs GS $8.66 and Street $8.54. Operating margin is guided to the mid-50% range vs Street 52.9%.
GS raises EPS estimates by ~11% on average. CY26E EPS goes to $27.00 from $26.30, CY27E to $50.30 from $43.75 and CY28E to $68.60 from $59.80.
GS cuts its 12-month price target to $900 from $960. It uses a 20x P/E, down from 24x because peer multiples are lower, on normalized EPS of $45.00 (up from $40.00).

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $900 from $960 as the P/E multiple falls to 20x from 24x on lower peer multiples. Normalized EPS rises to $45.00 from $40.00 on stronger revenue and gross margin trends.

sector_views.rationale: GS says shifting industry dynamics are likely to cap HDD multiples. Supply and demand are tight, but a smaller competitor (believed to be Toshiba) could add capacity.

earnings_insights: STX FQ1 (3Q26 column), reported 10/27: revenue $4.233bn vs GS $4.196bn and Street $4.141bn, up 61.0% y/y and 16.6% q/q.
STX FQ1 reported non-GAAP diluted EPS $7.68 vs GS est $7.59 and Street est $7.42. Gross margin was 57.8% and operating margin 50.7%.

STX FQ2 guidance (4Q26E column): revenue $4.70-4.90bn (midpoint $4.80bn, +71.2% y/y at midpoint). Non-GAAP EPS $9.00-9.40 (midpoint $9.20) vs GS est $8.66 and Street est $8.54. Operating margin is guided to mid-50%, vs Street est 52.9%.
Guidance assumptions: OpEx $300mn, tax rate 16%, share count 233mn.
GS new estimates, calendar year: 2026E non-GAAP EPS $27.00, revenue $15,887mn. 2027E EPS $50.30, revenue $24,242mn. 2028E EPS $68.60, revenue $30,789mn.
GS new estimates, fiscal year: FY27E EPS $38.52 (old $35.09) and FY28E EPS $58.45 (old $51.00). FY27E revenue is $20,393.7mn (old $18,864.5mn).
risk_factors: Difficulties qualifying HAMR at the major hyperscalers.
Lack of supply-side prudence from Seagate or the broader industry.
Potentially significant capacity additions by a smaller competitor (GS believes Toshiba) could disrupt supply/demand balance.
vol_and_positioning: Investor positioning in STX heading into the print was mixed, per GS investor conversations.
GS expects a modest decline in the stock after the print because expectations were elevated following Western Digital's strong report.

tension_points.bull_case: Management says customer demand will stay elevated for the foreseeable future. Supply/demand is tight, pricing per exabyte is up ~33% y/y and expected to hold through FY27, and HAMR drives raise capacity and margins.
tension_points.bear_case: A smaller competitor (GS believes Toshiba) could add significant capacity, and GS says shifting industry dynamics are likely to cap HDD multiples. Management acknowledged this only implicitly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Difficulties qualifying HAMR at major hyperscalers, or a lack of supply-side prudence from Seagate or the wider industry.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tight HDD supply/demand and the HAMR ramp support outsized earnings growth, though shifting industry dynamics cap multiples.
theme_stances.evidence: strong incremental margins, which are being bolstered by the company's HAMR technology ramp
